text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD alert — /v1/generate p95 latency 3.8s (threshold 1.2s), p99 12.4s. Error rate 5xx/timeout spike across us-west-2. Auto-sla alarms triggered.

anna_oncall: I'm on it. Paging SRE rotation. Any recent deploys?

deploy-bot: Deploy finished 00:07 UTC (~7m ago) — ref: feat/batching-optimizations @sha: f4b2c1a — rollout to prod canary=10%, global=100% started 00:03 UTC.

devon_sre: seeing large tail at the gateway — many requests hitting upstream model with long queue times, KV cache miss rate jumped ~x4. Trying to get traces.

leo_infra: pulling traces now. Gateway logs show connection timeout to runtime workers around 00:10 UTC. 504 spike correlates with that timeframe.

anna_oncall: can we isolate to model variant or the new kernel selection? Any canary vs global difference?

devon_sre: quick query: canary nodes (10%) show nominal latency. Global nodes that got the rollout show the spike. Suspect rollout switch at 00:03 applied a change to batching config.

sara_prod: just got a customer call — a handful of high-traffic customers seeing errors in region us-west-2. Maria from CS copied. Maria, collecting impacted customers now.

maria_cs: confirmed 3 customers reporting elevated 5xxs and timeouts, started incident emails, will update with customer-visible SLAs and time windows.

anna_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) pause rollout / revert to previous release 2) activate fallback routing to compatible smaller model 3) raise gateway timeout temporarily 4) notify customers. Devon, Leo — pick 1 and 2.

devon_sre: running revert now. Command:```bash
deployctl rollback --service=inference --to=release/e7a9 --namespace=prod
```

deploy-bot: Rollback started by devops at 00:14 UTC — job id rb-1923. Canary traffic cut, global rollback in progress.

leo_infra: Also enabling fallback route for critical tenants:```json
{"route_override": "model:llama-2-lite", "priority": 100}
```Applying to tenant routing for top 5 customers.

anna_oncall: aws autoscaling note — CPU/GPU utilization rose, but no OOM. Not scaling helpful for queue latency; it's likely batching config causing head-of-line blocking.

devon_sre: Observability update: after rollback initiated, p95 dropped from 3.8s -> 1.1s within ~45s. Error rate climbed briefly and then dropped.

maria_cs: sending interim message to impacted customers: "We detected a regression after a recent deploy affecting a subset of requests in us-west-2. We've rolled back the deploy and are monitoring. You may see transient 5xx/timeouts; apologies, more updates in 15m."

sara_prod: thanks. Please include estimated duration and whether any data loss.

maria_cs: no data loss observed, just increased latency and 5xx responses. Sending update now.

devon_sre: digging into the release diff — the batching change reduced max-batch-wait to 30ms and enabled continuous batching kernel for certain sequence lengths. Hypothesis: for long-tail requests the new kernel produced pathological queue behavior under our traffic distribution.

leo_infra: logs show many small requests kept waiting for long-running big requests in same batch; KV cache eviction rate spiked, causing repeated recompute and stalling.

anna_oncall: good detective work. Next: create short-lived guardrails so rollout doesn't re-trigger. Lock the release and set canary to 0.

devon_sre: lock in place, rollout paused. Also pushing a temporary config to gateway to increase idle conn timeout:```yaml
gateway:
  upstream_timeout: 30s  # was 10s
```Applying now.

incident-bot: Update: rollback rb-1923 succeeded at 00:16:22 UTC. Post-rollback checks green.

devon_sre: p95/p99 back to baseline (p95 0.9s, p99 1.6s). Error rate down to normal. Keeping additional monitoring for 30m.

anna_oncall: handoff in 30 minutes to night rotation — @devon_sre will take lead for postmortem. Please collect traces, timeline, and the minimal repro (traffic pattern + sequence length).

maria_cs: customers informed of resolution. Will open follow-up tickets for customers who asked for RCA.

sara_prod: any quick mitigations to avoid reoccurrence? A few ideas: conservative canary traffic rules, add batching integration tests with mixed-length synthetic traffic, and a circuit-breaker on new kernel paths.

devon_sre: agreed. I'll add a CanarySafety flag that forces bypass of the new kernel until perf gates pass. Also adding a runtime metric for per-batch composition so we can alert on skew.

leo_infra: schedule a postmortem war room tomorrow 15:00 UTC. Assigning devon_sre as owner.

devon_sre: assigned. Initial notes pinned to the incident doc. Will attach logs, perf diffs, and the exact config change that triggered the regression.

anna_oncall: thanks team. Final status: rollback completed; customer impact limited (roughly 6 minutes of elevated errors in us-west-2 affecting ~3 customers, transient 5xx/timeouts, no data loss). Monitoring continues. On-call handing to night in 30m.

deploy-bot: Note: rollout for feat/batching-optimizations has been marked blocked until postmortem completed.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident resolved (auto-close in 60m) — final classification: regression after deploy -> rollback mitigated. Postmortem owner: devon_sre.

anna_oncall: closing thread for now. Postmortem doc link will be posted here when ready. :thumbsup:
